issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts that omega_k = lambda_k^{-1/2}<W_Q, e_k> is a standard Wiener process under (i) and (ii) only, and the proof says this holds 'by definition'. Var<W_Q(t),e_k> = t<Q e_k,e_k>, which equals t*lambda_k only if e_k is an eigenvector of Q with eigenvalue lambda_k, i.e. only under (iii). Without (iii) (e.g. e_1=(f_1+f_2)/sqrt2) the variance is t(lambda_1+lambda_2)/(2 lambda_1), not t.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Move the standardness claim under the hypothesis that (iii) holds, or define omega_k with the normalisation <Q e_k,e_k>^{-1/2}.
issues.overall_effect: The statement of the lemma is false as stated when (iii) is dropped. Later results assume the full Assumption 2.1, so they are unaffected.
issues.title: Standard-Wiener property of omega_k claimed without the joint-eigenbasis hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis fix; every downstream use already assumes (iii).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the root-mean-square error (E|c_k - c~_k|^2)^{1/2} by sqrt(lambda_k)/Gamma(gamma) times an L^2 or L^p norm (with the factors (1+sqrt(log(t/h))) and mu_k^{-1/q}). Squaring gives lambda_k, delta^2 = (1+sqrt(log))^2, and mu_k^{-2/q} for the mean-square error. The theorem states the mean-square error with sqrt(lambda_k), delta (unsquared) and mu_k^{-1/q}. For lambda_k>1 or mu_k<1 the stated bound is smaller than what is proved. Theorem 3.9 and the proof of Lemma function_approximation use lambda_k and mu_k^{-2/q}, which confirms the mismatch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace sqrt(lambda_k) by lambda_k, delta_{gamma,h} by delta_{gamma,h}^2 and mu_k^{-1/q} by mu_k^{-2/q} in Theorem 3.4 and the two Corollaries, and add the missing 1/Gamma(gamma)^2 factor to the constants.
issues.overall_effect: The per-coefficient MSE bounds in Theorem 3.4 and the Corollaries that restate it are not established as written. Theorem 3.9 uses the correct lambda_k and mu_k^{-2/q}, so it is inconsistent with the theorem it claims to combine.
issues.title: Stated temporal MSE bound does not match what the proof gives (lambda_k vs sqrt(lambda_k), delta vs delta^2, mu_k^{-2/q} vs mu_k^{-1/q})
issues.why_classification: The proof already gives the correct squared bound; only the statements need local correction, and the rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: From xi_k >= C_Delta k^{2/d} one gets (kappa^2+xi_k)^alpha >= C_Delta^alpha k^{2 alpha/d} and (kappa^2+xi_k)^{-beta} <= C_Delta^{-beta} k^{-2 beta/d}. The proof instead uses C_Delta to the first power in both bounds. The correct constants are C_1 = r^{-1} C_Delta^alpha and C_2 = sigma r^{-gamma} C_Delta^{-beta}. The explicit constant in the corollary should then be sigma r^{gamma-1} C_Delta^{-(beta+(2gamma-1)alpha)}, not sigma r^{gamma-1} C_Delta^{2-2gamma}. The stated constant is wrong unless C_Delta=1 or alpha=beta=1. Remark 2 extends the corollary to closed manifolds, but there the lowest eigenvalue is 0 and xi_k >= C_Delta k^{2/d} fails at k=1, so the constants must be redone there as well.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute C_1 and C_2 with the correct powers, state the corrected explicit constant, and for closed manifolds use kappa^2+xi_k >= c k^{2/d} to cover xi_1=0.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate M^{-2 nu/d} is unaffected, but the explicit constant C in the corollary is false as stated, and Remark 2's extension to the sphere or closed manifolds inherits the problem.
issues.title: Wrong powers of C_Delta in the eigenvalue bounds and in the explicit constant of the Laplacian corollary
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation of constants; the theorem, rate and method survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, if $\theta \in [0,1]$ and $\gamma \leq 1$, or if $\theta \in [0,1)$, we have that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds ||Pi_0(g+alpha f)||^2 by comparing the three sums g_l^2 h_l, 2 alpha g_l f(s~_l) h_l and alpha^2 f(s~_l)^2 h_l term by term with the corresponding terms of ||g+alpha f||^2. The cross terms 2 alpha g_l ... have arbitrary sign, so a relation a ≲ b between the underlying positive quantities does not give 2 alpha g_l a ≲ 2 alpha g_l b. The inequality is reversed when alpha g_l < 0. In addition, the pointwise value (t_n - s~_l)^{gamma-1} (t_n - t_{l-1}) - (t_n - s~_l)^{gamma-1} (t_n - t_l) is replaced by the difference of the powers of t_n - t_{l-1} and t_n - t_l, using comparabilities of the two terms separately; this is not legitimate for a difference. The correct estimate is a uniform local norm-equivalence on span{1, f} over each cell, and it is not proved. The final case split also reads 'gamma <= 1' where gamma > 1 is needed for theta = 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a cell-wise estimate |g_l + alpha f(s~_l)|^2 h_l <= C ||g_l + alpha f||^2_{L^2(I_l)}, with C uniform in l via the comparability lemma and a scaling or compactness argument (separate treatment of l=n), then sum over cells.
issues.overall_effect: The mesh-uniform stability constant C_Pi for the piecewise-constant (left-point etc.) quadrature, on which the order-0 convergence corollary and the left-point numerics rely, is not established.
issues.title: Proof of L2-boundedness of Pi_0 compares indefinite-sign cross terms and subtracts comparabilities
issues.why_classification: The lemma is plausible and the repair is a contained new local argument (norm equivalence on a two-dimensional space with uniform constants), not a redesign.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we have convergence of $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} \lambda_k$ assuming only that $Q$ is bounded

issues.failure_explanation: A bounded inverse only means mu_k is bounded below by a positive constant. Summability of mu_k^{-1} means A^{-1} is trace class, which is much stronger. For the paper's operators mu_k ~ k^{2 alpha/d}, so sum mu_k^{-1} < infinity iff alpha > d/2. The paper's own sphere example (alpha = 0.5, d = 2) violates this. So 'in most practical applications' and 'assuming only that Q is bounded' are unsupported: C''_M need not stay bounded in M. The same paragraph also writes the improved constant with a square root, which contradicts the sum without a square root in Theorem 3.9.

failure_location.quote: In most practical applications $A$ will have bounded inverse, i.e., $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} < \infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the condition correctly (A^{-1} trace class, i.e. sum mu_k^{-1} < infinity, so alpha > d/2 for the Laplacian-based operators), drop the 'most practical applications' claim, and remove the stray square root.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the temporal error constant is uniformly bounded in M for large gamma under mild assumptions is not supported. The discussion of when the full scheme avoids M-dependent constants is misleading for the paper's operators with small alpha.
issues.title: Bounded inverse of A conflated with summable reciprocal eigenvalues; claimed boundedness of the temporal constant
issues.why_classification: Only discussion prose needs correcting; no theorem changes.

issues.failure_explanation: With alpha=0.5, kappa=2.828 (=sqrt 8) and gamma=1.5, the paper's formula gives r = r_t * 2.828/sqrt(8) = r_t. So r = 10.0 corresponds to r_t = 10, not 5.0. Equivalently, r_t = 5 would require r = 5. The other derived values (nu_t=1, nu_s=1, r_s=1, beta_s=0.5) are consistent with the formulas, so the stated r_t does not follow from the stated parameters.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct either r_t (to 10) or r (to 5) so that they agree with the reparametrisation formula.
issues.overall_effect: The reported temporal range of the simulated field is misreported by a factor of 2 relative to the paper's own parametrisation. No theorem is affected.
issues.title: Sphere experiment parameters inconsistent with the stated reparametrisation (r_t)
issues.why_classification: A local numeric inconsistency in an illustrative experiment; no formal result or guarantee depends on it.
